THOSE TWO REQUIREMENTS ARE MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE: the mask destroys the magnitude that encodes the draw count, so n is UNRECOVERABLE from `state >>> 0`. The only way to satisfy both as written is to add a per-draw counter. The builder found the contradiction and bridged it correctly with a Proxy wrapping every .random() -- and verified randomInt is counted through it, 10/10. MEASURED COST of the bridge, 5M draws x 5 trials, median: raw SeededRng 2.9454 ns/draw vs shipped Proxy counter 33.5467 ns/draw -- 11.4x, +30.6 ns/draw, allocating a fresh closure per draw on the sim's HOTTEST call site. Record it as such. === THE FIX, AND IT IS STRICTLY BETTER THAN WHAT WAS ASKED FOR === DO NOT COUNT DRAWS -- ASK WHETHER THE ACCUMULATOR IS STILL EXACT. The cliff IS the loss of integer exactness, so measure THAT directly instead of using draw count as a proxy for it. DIRECTOR-VERIFIED ARITHMETIC, independently recomputed rather than accepted: mulberry32's increment is 0x6D2B79F5 = 1831565813. 2^53 // 1831565813 = 4,917,758 exactly, matching the computed cliff. n*INC = 9007197429407254 <= 2^53 holds; (n+1)*INC = 9007199260973067 <= 2^53 FAILS. So Number.isSafeInteger(state) flips false ENTERING DRAW 4,917,759, while the first masked-vs-unmasked divergence was measured at 4,917,760. THE CHECK TRIPS EXACTLY ONE DRAW BEFORE THE FIRST REAL DIVERGENCE -- conservative, fails safe, no off-by-one exposure. State is monotonic, so a SINGLE END-OF-RUN check per stream is sound. ZERO per-draw cost. This is the same move already made elsewhere in this lane when observed SEQUENCES were compared instead of child seeds: measure the property you care about, not a quantity that stands in for it. === FENCE AMENDED, WHICH IS WHAT THE PM CORRECTLY REFUSED TO DO ON ITS OWN AUTHORITY === The atom's constraint read 'core change is limited to the single getState getter and NO other core surface'.
